title: Admit a rebuild's basis on a live store: local edits made after the rebuild must stay owed, not refuse the basis import
outcome: Admit a rebuild's basis on a live store: local edits made after the rebuild must stay owed, not refuse the basis import
acceptance: After `task-sync export --rebuild` is committed, `task-sync import --basis OWN_EXPORT/project.json` succeeds even when tasks were edited locally after the rebuild; those later local edits stay owed to the next export and are never treated as divergent planning against the store's own rebuild
The next ordinary `task-sync export` after that basis import takes the incremental route (no task_sync_commit_context_required) with a constant Git launch count
A behavioural CLI test reproduces it: rebuild, commit, a local edit, the basis import (passes), then an incremental export that writes the edited task
A genuine peer change to the same task between the rebuild and the import is still refused as divergent; this is not loosened
